prompt: The fee page asks for the full card number. The store app shows no fee.

choices.label: Pay. The app must be behind.
Close it. The app is the order.
Save the card for next time.

prompt: A leaked password with a new number on the end. What do attackers try first?

choices.label: A completely different phrase.
The leaked one, and small changes.
Only passwords from ten years ago.

prompt: Friends-only, and the badge is still in the photo. What is the risk?

choices.label: Friends cannot share a picture.
A screenshot leaves the group.
The risk is posting on a weekend.

prompt: You changed the Wi-Fi password. The admin password is still the one on the sticker.

choices.label: The network is finished.
The admin door is still open.
A short Wi-Fi name closes it.

prompt: You were expecting a parcel. A text says it is held.

choices.label: Expecting it makes the text real.
Expecting it is why you check the app.
A small fee means it is real.

prompt: The streaming password is new and unique. Work still uses the old pattern.

choices.label: One site was enough.
Work still has the leaked twin.
Wait for work to force a change.

prompt: The board in the photo shows a guest password. You already posted.

choices.label: Leave it. Few people will zoom.
Take it down, and tell the desk.
Crop it now. The post already went.

prompt: Work traffic crosses the home router some days. The firmware is from years ago.

choices.label: Old firmware is fine if it is fast.
Update it before you trust it.
Turn the router off overnight.

prompt: Three more texts arrive after you reply. What did the reply do?

choices.label: It stopped a real courier.
It showed the number is read.
It paid the fee.

prompt: Where should the new unique passwords live?

choices.label: In your head, one pattern.
In a password manager.
On a note in the laptop bag.
